title: Friendship and Feelings
description: Ten short stories, diary entries and emails about old and new friends, small misunderstandings, missing home and helping others.

lessons.title: Hello Again
lessons.summary: Anna meets her best friend from high school again in a coffee shop after many years.
lessons.text:
Anna is 38 years old, and she works as an editor at a small newspaper in Boston. As an editor, she reads other people's stories and makes them better. Every Saturday morning, she goes to the same coffee shop near her apartment, orders a cup of tea and reads a novel.

Last Saturday, Anna was reading her novel when a woman stopped next to her table.

"Hello," the woman said. "I'm sorry, but are you Anna Brooks?"

Anna looked up. The woman had short dark hair and a warm smile. For a moment, Anna didn't know her. Then she remembered. "Kate? Kate Miller? Hello! I can't believe it!"

Kate had been Anna's best friend in high school. When they were 16, they had promised to be friends forever. But after school, Kate had moved to California with her family, and the two friends had slowly lost contact.

"Please, sit down," Anna said. She was so excited that she almost dropped her cup. Kate ordered a tea too, and the two women talked for hours. They had plenty to talk about.

Kate told Anna that she had come back to Boston 2 months before. "I've been living here since August," she said. "I always thought you were somewhere in this city, but I didn't know how to find you."

"What do you do now?" Anna asked.

Kate smiled. "I write novels. My first novel is coming out next year."

Anna laughed. "And I'm an editor! If you ever need an editor, you know where to find me."

Then a man came into the coffee shop with a little girl. Kate introduced them. "This is my husband, Paul, and our daughter, Lily." Anna introduced herself, and Lily smiled.

Before they left, Kate and Anna exchanged phone numbers. "Let's meet here every Saturday," Kate said. "We still have plenty to talk about." Anna agreed. She felt excited and happy. Maybe some friends really are friends forever.

Questions:
Where does Anna work?
Anna works as an editor at a small newspaper in Boston.
What does Anna do every Saturday morning?
She goes to a coffee shop near her apartment, orders a cup of tea and reads a novel.
Who said hello to Anna?
Kate, her best friend from high school, said hello to her.
What had Anna and Kate promised when they were 16?
They had promised to be friends forever.
Where did Kate think Anna was?
She thought Anna was somewhere in Boston.
Who did Kate introduce to Anna?
Kate introduced her husband, Paul, and their daughter, Lily.
What did Kate and Anna decide to do?
They decided to meet at the coffee shop every Saturday.

lessons.title: The Missing Package
lessons.summary: Emma thinks her roommate has taken her package, but she waits, talks to her kindly and learns what really happened.
lessons.text:
Emma and Jen have been sharing an apartment for 2 years. They rent it together and split the rent: each of them pays an equal part every month. Usually, they get along very well.

Last Tuesday, Emma came home from work late. She was waiting for an important package: a new computer for her job. The website said that the package had been delivered at 2 in the afternoon. But when Emma looked outside the door, there was no package.

Then she went into the living room. The living room was a mess. There were cups on the table, shoes on the floor and papers everywhere. Jen wasn't home.

Emma felt angry. "Jen hasn't cleaned anything," she thought. "She hasn't even washed the cups. And where is my package? Maybe Jen took it and forgot about it." She wanted to send Jen an angry message. But she stopped. "I've had a long day, and when I'm tired, I get angry too fast," she thought. "I should wait and talk to her later."

At 7 in the evening, there was a knock at the door. Emma opened it. It was Mrs. Wood, the old woman who lives next door. She was holding a big box. "Hello, Emma," she said. "This package came for you this afternoon. Nobody was home, so the driver knocked on my door and gave it to me."

Emma thanked her. She felt a little bad about her angry thoughts.

An hour later, Jen came home. "I'm sorry about the mess," she said. "I had to leave fast this morning because my mother called. She needed help with something. I'll clean everything now."

Emma decided to be honest. "To be honest, I was angry when I came home," she said. "I thought you had taken my package. I'm glad I didn't send you an angry message."

Jen laughed. "Thank you for being honest. Next time, just call me, and I'll tell you what happened." Then they cleaned the living room together, and the mess was gone in 20 minutes.

Questions:
How do Emma and Jen split the rent?
Each of them pays an equal part every month.
What package was Emma waiting for?
She was waiting for a new computer for her job.
Why did Emma feel angry?
The living room was a mess, and she thought Jen had taken her package.
Who knocked on the door at 7 in the evening?
Mrs. Wood, the old woman who lives next door, knocked on the door.
Why was the living room a mess?
Jen had to leave fast in the morning because her mother needed help.
What did Emma and Jen do at the end?
They cleaned the living room together.

lessons.title: A Diary Far from Home
lessons.summary: In her diary, a Spanish student in Chicago writes about missing home and finding a new friend.
lessons.text:
October 3

My name is Lucia, and I have been living in Chicago for 5 weeks now. I came here from Valencia, in Spain, to study for one academic year at the university. My native language is Spanish. But here, everyone speaks so fast!

Today I missed home a lot. In Valencia, my apartment is 10 minutes from the ocean. Every evening, I used to walk by the ocean with my sister. Here, there is a big lake, but it is not the same as the ocean. The climate is different too. In Valencia, the climate is warm. Here, it is already cold in October, and people say the winter will be very hard.

Tonight I looked at the moon from my window. I thought: my family can see the same moon. That made me feel a little better. I have a small Spanish flag on the wall above my bed. When I look at the flag, I think of my mother and father.

October 10

Today something good happened. In my English class, the teacher asked us to give a short lesson about our native countries. I gave a lesson about Valencia. I showed pictures of the ocean, the old city and our food. After the lesson, a girl from my class came to talk to me. Her name is Megan, and she is learning Spanish! "Your lesson was great," she said. "Would you help me with my Spanish? I can help you with your English."

We had coffee together after class. Megan has a soft voice and a kind smile. She speaks Spanish very well. We decided to meet twice a week: one hour in English and one hour in Spanish.

October 17

Megan and I met 3 times this week. Last night, she took me to the lake. The moon was big, and the sand was soft under our feet. It was not the ocean, but it was beautiful. If I were at home, I would be by the ocean with my sister. But tonight I was happy here, with a new friend. The academic year is long, but maybe it won't feel so long now.

Questions:
Why did Lucia come to Chicago?
She came to study for one academic year at the university.
What is Lucia's native language?
Her native language is Spanish.
How is the climate in Chicago different from the climate in Valencia?
In Valencia, the climate is warm, but in Chicago it is already cold in October.
What does Lucia have on the wall above her bed?
She has a small Spanish flag.
Who did Lucia meet after her lesson about Valencia?
She met Megan, a girl from her class who is learning Spanish.

lessons.title: The First Weeks at Work
lessons.summary: Tom starts a job at a steel company, and the worker who helps him becomes his first friend in the city.
lessons.text:
Tom was 24 when he got a job at a steel company. The company was in the industrial part of the city, near the river. It made steel parts for cars and trains. Tom had never worked in an industrial building before, so he was a little worried on his first day.

His manager, Mrs. Diaz, met him at the door. "Welcome, Tom," she said. "For the first 2 weeks, Marcus will assist you. He has been working here for 10 years, and he knows everything."

Marcus was a big man with a big smile. "Don't worry," he said. "The initial weeks are always the hardest. After that, it gets easier."

First, Marcus explained the safety regulations. "There are a lot of regulations here," he said, "and every regulation is important. For example, you must always wear safety glasses and strong shoes."

Then Marcus showed Tom the procedure for the big electric machines. "Before you start an electric machine, you check it," he said. "When you finish, you turn it off. Every step of the procedure matters."

On his third day, Tom made an error. He forgot to turn off an electric machine before he cleaned it. Marcus saw it and turned the machine off. Tom felt bad. "I'm sorry," he said.

Marcus wasn't angry. "Everyone makes errors at the start," he said. "I made the same error in my first week. The important thing is to learn from it." Then he gave Tom a useful idea: "Say the steps of the procedure out loud. It's simple, but it's really useful."

Tom tried it, and it worked. He never made that error again.

Every day at lunch, Tom and Marcus ate together. They talked about football, music and their families. One Friday, Marcus invited Tom to play football with his friends in the park. Tom enjoyed playing with them very much.

After the initial 2 weeks, Tom didn't need help anymore. But he still ate lunch with Marcus every day. "You assisted me with the work," Tom said, "but you also became my first friend in this city." Marcus laughed. "That's not in the regulations," he said, "but it's the best part of the job."

Questions:
What did Tom's company make?
It made steel parts for cars and trains.
Who assisted Tom in his initial weeks?
Marcus assisted him. He had been working at the company for 10 years.
What did Marcus explain first?
He explained the safety regulations.
What error did Tom make on his third day?
He forgot to turn off an electric machine before he cleaned it.
What useful idea did Marcus give Tom?
He told Tom to say the steps of the procedure out loud.

lessons.title: Thanksgiving on Oak Lane
lessons.summary: Sam helps Mrs. Hall, who lives next door and is sad after she hurts her leg, and invites her for Thanksgiving.
lessons.text:
Sam is 15, and he lives with his mother in a small house on Oak Lane. The woman next door, Mrs. Hall, is 78 years old. She has lived on Oak Lane for 50 years, and she loves working in her garden. Every morning, she used to stand at her gate and say hello to everyone who walked down the lane.

But in November, Sam didn't see Mrs. Hall at her gate for a whole week. Then one afternoon, he saw her by the window. She was sitting in a chair with wheels. Sam knocked on her door.

"Oh, Sam," Mrs. Hall said. "I've had a terrible week. I fell on the ice and cracked a bone in my leg. The doctor says my leg will take 2 months to get better. Until then, I have to use this chair with wheels."

She looked very sad. "And my son can't come for Thanksgiving this year. He lives in Texas, and he has to work. I've been sitting alone in this house for days. It's terrible."

That evening, Sam talked to his mother. "Mrs. Hall needs help," he said. "Can we do something?" His mother agreed at once.

The next morning, Sam started helping. Every day before school, he grabbed the newspaper from Mrs. Hall's gate and brought it inside. After school, he did her shopping. On nice afternoons, he pushed her chair down the lane, so she could see the trees and talk to people. Mrs. Hall enjoyed these walks very much.

On Thanksgiving, Sam and his mother cooked a big turkey. Sam put on his coat, grabbed a warm hat for Mrs. Hall and went next door. He pushed her chair through her gate and into their house. The three of them ate turkey and potatoes together and talked for hours.

"I thought this Thanksgiving would be terrible," Mrs. Hall said. "But it's one of the best ones I've ever had." In January, her leg was strong again, and she was back at her gate every morning, saying hello to everyone on Oak Lane.

Questions:
Where does Sam live?
He lives with his mother in a small house on Oak Lane.
What happened to Mrs. Hall?
She fell on the ice and cracked a bone in her leg.
Why was Mrs. Hall sad?
She couldn't walk well, and her son couldn't come for Thanksgiving.
What did Sam do every day before school?
He grabbed the newspaper from Mrs. Hall's gate and brought it inside.
What did Sam and his mother cook on Thanksgiving?
They cooked a big turkey.

lessons.title: The Painting Class
lessons.summary: Grace joins a painting class, makes a new friend there and wins a prize with her friend's help.
lessons.text:
After Grace stopped working, she had a lot of free time, but she didn't see many people. Her daughter said, "Mom, why don't you take a class? You used to love painting." So Grace signed up for a painting class at the community center.

In the first class, there were 8 students. They sat in a circle around a table with flowers on it. Grace sat next to a woman named Rosa, who was about her age. Rosa had been taking the class for a year.

"Today, just paint what you see," said the teacher, Mr. Ortiz. Grace was worried. She hadn't painted anything for 30 years. But she started slowly, and soon she forgot about everything else.

At the end of the class, Mr. Ortiz walked around the circle and looked at every painting. He stopped at Grace's painting. "This is excellent," he said. "Look at the combination of colors: the dark blue and the soft yellow. It's a lovely combination. You have real talent."

Grace's face turned red. "I don't know about talent," she said. "I just enjoy painting."

After class, Rosa invited her for coffee. They talked about their children, their gardens and their favorite painters. From that day on, they always sat next to each other in the circle.

In the spring, Mr. Ortiz told the class about a painting competition in the town. "Anyone can participate," he said. "The first prize is $500, and the best paintings will hang in the library for a month."

"You should participate," Rosa told Grace. "With your talent, you could win a prize." At first, Grace didn't want to, but Rosa helped her choose a painting: a picture of the river with a small red bird in the upper corner. "That bird in the upper corner is fantastic," Rosa said. "It's the first thing everyone sees."

Grace didn't win first prize, but she won third prize, and her painting hung in the library. Rosa came with her to see it. "Fantastic!" Rosa said. "I'm so proud of you."

Grace smiled. "Thank you for telling me to participate. Without you, I wouldn't be here today."

Questions:
Why did Grace start a painting class?
She had a lot of free time, and her daughter told her to take a class.
Where did the students sit?
They sat in a circle around a table with flowers on it.
What did Mr. Ortiz say about Grace's painting?
He said it was excellent and that she had real talent.
What was in the upper corner of Grace's painting?
There was a small red bird in the upper corner.
What prize did Grace win?
She won third prize, and her painting hung in the library.

lessons.title: A Proper Suit
lessons.summary: A young man needs a suit for his best friend's wedding, and the old tailor who makes it turns out to know his family.
lessons.text:
In June, my best friend Mark asked me to be the best man at his wedding. I was very happy, but I had a problem: I didn't have a proper suit. I only had work clothes.

My mother said, "Go to Mr. Rossi. He's the best tailor in town. He made your father's wedding suit."

Mr. Rossi's shop is small. It is on Main Street, between a bank and a women's clothes store. When I opened the door, an old man in a gray cap looked up from his table. "Hello," he said. "How can I help you?"

I told him about the wedding and gave him my name. "Your father is Joe Green?" he asked. "I remember him! I made his suit 30 years ago." He came and shook my hand.

Then Mr. Rossi measured me with great care. "Your arms are 25 inches long," he said, "and your legs are 32 inches. A proper suit must fit well. Even one inch is important."

"Can you finish it in 3 weeks?" I asked. "The wedding is on July 10."

"I guarantee it," he said. "In 40 years, I have never been late for a wedding."

2 weeks later, he called me. "There is a small delay," he said. "The material for your suit is coming from Italy, and the delivery has been delayed by 3 days. But don't worry. My guarantee is still good. You will have your suit before the wedding."

He kept his promise. On July 8, I went back to the shop and tried on the suit. It fit very well. Mr. Rossi took off his cap and smiled. "Now you look like your father," he said.

At the wedding, many people asked me about my suit, and I told them about Mr. Rossi. A week later, I brought him a photo from the wedding. He put it on the wall of his shop, next to an old photo of my father. We shook hands, and he said, "Come and visit any time. Joe's son is my friend too."

Questions:
Who is Mr. Rossi?
He is the best tailor in town.
Why did the writer need a proper suit?
His best friend Mark asked him to be the best man at his wedding.
Where is Mr. Rossi's shop?
It is on Main Street, between a bank and a women's clothes store.
Who did Mr. Rossi remember?
He remembered the writer's father. He had made his wedding suit 30 years ago.
Why was there a delay?
The material for the suit was coming from Italy, and the delivery was delayed by 3 days.
Did Mr. Rossi keep his guarantee?
Yes. The suit was ready before the wedding, and it fit very well.

lessons.title: The Friday Book Club
lessons.summary: A book club of old friends grows too big for its room and finds a fair answer together.
lessons.text:
The Friday Book Club started 10 years ago with 4 friends who loved reading. Now the club consists of 22 members. They meet every Friday evening in a small room at the town library, talk about a book and drink coffee together. Many members have become close friends.

The club is very democratic. Every member has one vote, and the club decides everything together. The president is Helen, and the vice president is her friend George. As vice president, George helps Helen plan the meetings.

This year, there was a problem. The room at the library has a capacity of 20 people, but the club had 22 members. At some meetings, people had to stand.

Helen and George proposed a reform. "We have 2 ideas," Helen said at a meeting. "First, we want to move to the big room at the community center. Its capacity is 50 people. Second, we want to meet on Thursdays, because the big room is free only on Thursdays."

Not everyone liked the proposed reform. An older member, Mr. Kent, stood up. "I'd like to protest," he said. "I have been coming here on Fridays for 10 years. On Thursdays I visit my sister. If we met on Thursdays, I couldn't come anymore."

Nobody got angry. Helen thanked him. "That's why we vote," she said. "It's a democratic club, and every opinion matters."

George had another idea. "What if we do the reform in 2 phases?" he said. "In the first phase, we move to the big room, but only on the Fridays when it's free. In the second phase, in the spring, we talk about the day again."

Everyone voted. 21 members voted for George's plan, and Mr. Kent voted for it too. "Now I don't need to protest," he said with a smile.

The first phase went well. In the big room, there was plenty of space, and 5 new members joined. In April, the club even took part in a regional book festival for the towns in the area. At the regional festival, Helen gave a short talk about the club. "We read books together," she said, "but the most important thing is that we are friends."

Questions:
How many members does the club consist of?
The club consists of 22 members.
Why did the club have a problem?
The room has a capacity of 20 people, but the club had 22 members.
What reform did Helen and George propose?
They proposed moving to the big room at the community center and meeting on Thursdays.
Why did Mr. Kent protest?
He visits his sister on Thursdays, so he couldn't come to the club on Thursdays.
What happened in the first phase?
The club moved to the big room on Fridays, and 5 new members joined.

lessons.title: An Email to an Old Friend
lessons.summary: Ben asks his old friend Laura for advice about a job offer, and she answers with a long, kind email.
lessons.text:
Hi Laura,

How are you? I need your advice, because you have always been honest with me.

As you know, I have been working at Bright, a small shop that fixes phones and computers, for 6 years. I love it there. I fix all kinds of electronic things, and my boss, Mr. Fox, is like a second father to me. But the shop is having a hard time. People buy new electronic things instead of fixing old ones, and the shop's sales have declined a lot this year. The shop still generates enough money to pay us, but not much more.

Last week, a massive electronic company in Seattle offered me a job. The wage is much higher: it is almost twice my wage now. But I would have to move, and I don't know anyone in Seattle.

I don't know what to do. If you were me, what would you do?

Ben

Dear Ben,

Thank you for your email. I'm happy you wrote to me.

First, I think it depends on what is important to you. If money were the most important thing, I would say: go to Seattle. A higher wage is useful, and a massive company can teach you a lot.

But you said you love your job, and you love the people. That is not entirely about money. In my opinion, the good people around you are the best assets in life. You can find a job anywhere, but you can't find a boss like Mr. Fox anywhere.

Also, have you talked to Mr. Fox? Maybe he has some ideas. The shop's sales have declined, but maybe you could help it generate more money. For example, you could teach classes on how to fix phones. Your talent with people is one of your biggest assets too.

I'm not saying you should decline the offer. The decision is entirely yours, and it depends only on you. But before you decline or say yes, please talk to Mr. Fox.

Whatever you decide, I'm always here for you.

Your friend,
Laura

Questions:
Where has Ben been working for 6 years?
He has been working at Bright, a small shop that fixes phones and computers.
Why is the shop having a hard time?
People buy new electronic things instead of fixing old ones, so the sales have declined.
What did the massive company in Seattle offer Ben?
It offered him a job with a much higher wage.
What does Laura say Ben can't find anywhere?
She says he can't find a boss like Mr. Fox anywhere.
What does Laura tell Ben to do before he decides?
She tells him to talk to Mr. Fox.

lessons.title: The View from the Peak
lessons.summary: After a ruined weekend plan, Mia climbs a hill with her friend Leo and feels better at the top.
lessons.text:
Mia had been looking forward to the concert for months. She had bought the tickets in January, and she was going to go with her sister. But on Friday afternoon, the concert was called off because of a storm. Then her sister got sick too. "My weekend is ruined," Mia thought. She was tired after a long week at work, and now she felt sad as well.

That evening, her friend Leo called her, and Mia told him everything. "Don't let one bad day ruin your whole weekend," Leo said. "Let's climb Bear Hill tomorrow. The view from the peak is lovely, and the weather will be good."

"I'm too tired," Mia said.

"You don't have to do anything," Leo said. "I'll be prepared. I'll bring water, food and warm coats. Just wear good shoes."

At 7 the next morning, Leo was at her door. He really was prepared: he had a big bag with everything they needed. They drove to Bear Hill and started walking. The path went up and up. The wind was cold, and soon Mia's ears were red. Leo gave her his hat. "Pull it down over your ears," he said.

After 2 hours, they reached the peak. Mia stopped and looked around. She could see the whole valley: green fields, a small lake and their town far below. "It's lovely," she said. She didn't feel tired anymore.

They sat on a rock at the peak and ate their food. Leo didn't talk much. He just sat next to her. His quiet presence made Mia feel safe and happy.

Before they left, Leo took a photo of Mia at the peak. "This is proof," he said. "Proof that your weekend wasn't ruined."

Mia laughed. That evening, she sent the photo to her sister with a message: "My weekend wasn't ruined. Leo's presence made it one of the best days of the year."

Questions:
Why did Mia think her weekend was ruined?
The concert was called off because of a storm, and her sister got sick.
What did Leo say he would bring?
He said he would bring water, food and warm coats.
Why did Leo give Mia his hat?
The wind was cold, and her ears were red.
What could Mia see from the peak?
She could see green fields, a small lake and their town far below.
What did Leo say the photo was?
He said it was proof that her weekend wasn't ruined.
